newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pratt&Whitney in Airbus A340 engine talks.
newsitem.headline: Pratt&Whitney in Airbus A340 engine talks.

text.p: U.S. aero-engine maker Pratt & Whitney said on Wednesday it is in talks with European consortium Airbus for a potential contract to supply motors for a stretched version of the long-range A340 wide-body jet.
"We are in the process of negotiating the deal," P&W's president of large commercial engines, Robert Wolfe, told Reuters at the margins of a news conference.
P&W, a United Technologies unit, is bidding against Rolls-Royce Plc to power the four-engined A340-600 "stretched" jet, after Airbus Industrie and GE lapsed an exclusive agreement for negotiations.
Wolfe said P&W would consider offering the commercial terms needed, short of harming its own business interest, to win the airbus engine contract.
"We believe if we enter as a total partnership with Airbus, we become part of Airbus... including whatever Airbus needs to sell that aircraft with our product on it," Wolfe said.

Airbus and GE broke off talks after the U.S. firm failed to make the commercial concessions Airbus was looking for in return for an exclusive agreement, Airbus Managing Director Jean Pierson said in February.
P&W would offer a version of its PW4000 family, with thrust between 70,000-80,000 pounds.
Rolls has said it was considering developing a version of its Trent turbofan for the A340 but would need other planes to sell to, besides the A340, to recover the development costs.

Wolfe said P&W would offer a variant of its PW4000 family or build a new engine for the Airbus A3XX 555-seater project, but was waiting for Airbus to decide whether it wants a new product or a derivative.
The A340-600 would seat 375 passengers and rival Boeing's 777 giant twinjet.
